OQ-9 STAGE-1 FREE-BIGRAM TWIN REGISTRATION (2026-10-01, pre-run; a DATED
AMENDMENT to the OQ-9 STAGE-1 block above, written BEFORE any readout of
it ran on either S3 harvest; the critic's design round is recorded at the
end of this block; the registered runs launch only after the freeze
commit):
- PROVENANCE. The one BLOCKING objection of the F-26 landing critic
  (2026-09-15, OUTCOME above, "SCOPE OF THAT SENTENCE"): F-26's free arm is a
  ONE-TOKEN table of tokens[t]; the previous token tokens[t-1] is exactly as
  free to the decoder and is not in the baseline, and the data say gate 0
  of OLMoE routes primarily on it (per-gate ADDRESS-BEYOND-TOKEN +0.221 /
  +0.224 at gate 0; the critic's val-only diagnostic 0.813 / 0.798 for a
  zero-fit table keyed on the previous token against 0.672 / 0.656 keyed on
  the current one, at gate 0). The OUTCOME names "the equal-dims free-bigram
  twin TABLE(tokens[t]) ++ TABLE(tokens[t-1]) ++ bias against HISTORY_TOK at
  B = 16, j = 1" as the next rung, "registered with its prediction pinned
  before the read — the critic's: the margin drops to or below the +0.05
  floor, driven by gate 0". The operator chose it as the first research
  change through the harness lane on 2026-10-01 ("confirm", after the
  assistant's proposal). It is a POST-HOC DIAGNOSTIC on test rows the
  stage-1 instrument and the critic's recompute have already read (the
  F-24 twin-inertness precedent: registered before THIS readout runs, on
  an already-read test set, and said so). NON-CRITERION for every
  mechanical label in the record: F-26's stage label and four readings were
  computed on the registered arms and stand as computed; no K-* status, no
  F-15 / F-17 / F-24 / F-25 sentence moves. ONE pinned consequence: a dated
  STATUS line under F-26 on the standing of its sideband sentence, per the
  branches below (a dated line, never a rewrite — the 2026-08-31 rule).
- QUESTION. How much of F-26's ADDRESS-BEYOND-TOKEN margin (+0.1032
  [+0.0926, +0.1146] primary / +0.1072 [+0.0952, +0.1206] replication at
  B = 16, j = 1; arms free_tok 0.8111 / 0.8036, history 0.8064 / 0.8056,
  history_tok 0.9143 / 0.9108) is free token-history information that a
  one-token table cannot encode? Put the previous token into the free
  baseline at EQUAL DIMS and re-read the margin; beside it, read what the
  address stream adds OVER the free bigram (the F-24 shape: the address
  block against the strengthened free baseline).
- THE FROZEN INSTRUMENT. tools/run_prefetch_readouts.py (sha
  8529532d4d78..., attested by both committed stage-1 payloads) is imported
  by bare module name and never edited; the new tool refuses to run unless
  its LF-normalised bytes still hash to that sha (the F-25 amended-
  instrument precedent). Its sha-bound S3Data loader, its leave-one-prompt-
  out TABLE encoding, its ridge / top-B / per-prompt machinery and its
  bootstrap helpers are reused, nothing re-derived; the test suite asserts
  the new tool's TABLE_CUR, pair tables and marginal equal Stage1.fit's to
  the integer on a fixture harvest.
- DATA. The committed S3 harvests exactly as stage 1 opened them (PRIMARY
  results/real/harvest_moe moe_s0..s7, the verdict harvest; REPLICATION
  harvest_moe_r moe_s8..s11, a SEED replication on the same prompts; split
  prompt_idx % 7; readers fit on train pooled over seeds, lambda selected on
  val, every number read on the 30 TEST prompts). POSITIONS: the BIGRAM
  positions, anchors t with t >= 1 and t + 1 < row length (tokens[t-1] and
  S[t+1] both exist), horizon j = 1 only; EVERY arm is read on these
  positions, so per-prompt trials are equal across arms. The committed
  stage-1 cells are NOT reused as numbers — the frozen state rows pool over
  t = 0 too and cannot be restricted — so history, free_tok and history_tok
  are RE-TRAINED here on the bigram positions, and the re-measured
  ADDRESS-BEYOND-TOKEN is a PRECONDITION (below) that the re-trained readers
  reproduce the committed cell.
- INDEX CONVENTION: the frozen one (forward t has INPUT tokens[t-1], OUTPUT
  p_t and routing S[t]; tokens[t] is sampled from p_t; at anchor t the
  decoder holds S[t], tokens[t] AND tokens[t-1]; the target is S[t+1]).
- TABLES (train-fit; every table block is read LEAVE-ONE-PROMPT-OUT at
  train rows exactly as the frozen instrument reads its TABLE; val and test
  rows read the full train table; a key with no train count at a gate takes
  MARGINAL's frequencies at the j = 1 targets, the frozen fallback):
  TABLE_CUR(x) = the frozen TABLE, train conditional expert frequencies of
  S[t+1] keyed on tokens[t] = x, built over the frozen instrument's own
  j = 1 train positions (t = 0 included); TABLE_PREV(x) = train conditional
  expert frequencies of S[t+1] keyed on tokens[t-1] = x, built over the
  bigram train positions. TWO FREE ENCODINGS of the previous token are
  carried, both 1024-dim, because the critic's one-line design admits both
  readings: (b) prev_table = TABLE_PREV(tokens[t-1]), target-aligned, the
  critic's diagnostic table; (a) cur_table_at_prev = TABLE_CUR(tokens[t-1]),
  the frozen table read at the previous token (its train routing profile
  for the forward it fed, an estimate of S[t]). Either block also carries
  the previous token's IDENTITY as a fingerprint to the extent its per-key
  vectors are distinct (the same channel TABLE_CUR(tokens[t]) gives the
  F-26 free arm); that identity is free information and is meant to be in
  the baseline. Two qualifications (critic design round): a linear reader
  on a 1024-dim table vector cannot resolve a 50,304-token identity, so
  the channel is partial on the real harvests (the 12-token fixture in
  the tests overstates it and is not cited for them); and S[t]'s own
  multi-hot is plausibly a fingerprint of tokens[t-1] at the early gates
  (the gate-0 margin +0.221 / +0.224), so a SIGNAL on D_add may include
  previous-token IDENTITY that the routing code exposes and the table
  does not. The outcome text therefore never calls D_add "context"; the
  rung that would separate identity from context is a pair-keyed or
  identity-resolving free encoding, named under CONSEQUENCES as unrun.
- DESIGN: one float64 Gram over the bigram train positions of
  [S[t] multi-hot (1024) ++ TABLE_CUR(tokens[t]) (1024) ++
  TABLE_PREV(tokens[t-1]) (1024) ++ TABLE_CUR(tokens[t-1]) (1024) ++ bias],
  every arm a slice (so all arms share positions exactly). ARMS (dims):
  history = S[t] (1025); free_tok = TABLE_CUR(tokens[t]) (1025), the F-26
  free arm; history_tok = S[t] ++ TABLE_CUR(tokens[t]) (2049), the F-26
  address arm; free_bigram_b = TABLE_CUR(tokens[t]) ++ (b) (2049);
  free_bigram_a = TABLE_CUR(tokens[t]) ++ (a) (2049); FREE_BIGRAM = the one
  of these two whose val-best pooled hit rate at B = 16 is higher (jointly
  with its lambda; ties keep (b)) — THE equal-dims twin of history_tok;
  history_bigram_b / history_bigram_a = S[t] ++ the matching free bigram's
  blocks (3073); HISTORY_BIGRAM = the one matching FREE_BIGRAM's encoding;
  free_all = TABLE_CUR(tokens[t]) ++ (b) ++ (a) (3073, reported);
  history_all = S[t] ++ free_all's blocks (4097, reported). Readers:
  closed-form ridge in float64, every coordinate incl. the bias regularised
  alike; one lambda per arm selected on val from the frozen grid {0.1, 1,
  10, 100, 1000, 1e4, 1e5} (strict >, ties keep the smaller; grid-edge
  flagged); resident set at gate l = the B largest predicted scores among
  that gate's 64 (ties by expert id ascending, stable sort); hit rate as
  the frozen instrument counts it. Val is read at every lambda; TEST is
  read at the selected lambdas only. Budgets B in {8, 16, 32}; B = 16 is
  the label budget, 8 and 32 reported.
- READOUTS at B = 16, paired per prompt on identical positions, cluster
  bootstrap over the 30 test prompts (sideband.stats.paired_cluster_delta_ci,
  n_boot 2000, seed 0), readings by the frozen rule (SIGNAL iff CI95 lower
  > 0 and point >= +0.05, the pinned materiality floor; NEGATIVE iff CI95
  upper < 0; else NOT-SHOWN):
  PRECONDITION  ADDRESS-BEYOND-TOKEN re-measured = history_tok - free_tok on
                the bigram positions; |re-measured - committed (+0.1032
                primary, +0.1072 replication, read by the tool from the
                committed payload, its sha recorded and re-read by
                --conclude-from)| <= 0.01, else REMEASURE-INVALID (no
                further label on that harvest). The tolerance is a
                gross-breakage check, calibrated: the stage-1 fourth
                smoke (h) read +0.1475 [+0.1334, +0.1616] on shard s8's
                re-split val prompts and this registration's smoke
                re-measures +0.1474 [+0.1334, +0.1612] on the same rows
                less their t = 0 anchors (gap 0.0001); dropping t = 0
                removes about 0.41% of train and 0.40% of test positions
                (one anchor per row against the committed position
                counts), which bounds its effect near 0.004 even in the
                extreme; BLAS summation order can move a near-tied top-B
                boundary by less.
  GATE  D_eq  = history_tok - FREE_BIGRAM (equal dims, 2049 vs 2049): the
                critic's named readout — does the address block beat a free
                block of equal dimension?
  D_add       = HISTORY_BIGRAM - FREE_BIGRAM (3073 vs 2049): what the
                address stream adds OVER the free bigram — the direct
                "beyond free" analogue of ADDRESS-BEYOND-TOKEN with the
                baseline strengthened.
  BIGRAM GAIN = FREE_BIGRAM - free_tok: what the free previous token adds;
                per gate it IS the per-gate drop of the margin (both arms
                share history_tok), so the critic's "driven by gate 0"
                sub-clause is scored two ways, both point comparisons with
                no per-gate bootstrap: (i) gate 0 has the largest per-gate
                bigram gain (an exact float tie would keep the lower gate
                id, a case not expected to arise), and (ii) gate 0's SHARE
                of the summed per-gate gain, reported beside the cap the
                critic derived — every gate has equal trials, so the
                pooled gain is the mean of the sixteen per-gate gains and
                gate 0 alone can add at most (1 - free_tok at gate 0) / 16
                = (1 - 0.6763) / 16 = 0.020 to it on the primary; a D_eq at
                or below +0.05 therefore needs a pooled gain of at least
                0.053, of which at least 62% must come from gates 1-15.
  TWIN EXEMPTION. D_add is a "B adds over A" readout and carries no
                destroyed twin of the address block, against the house
                rule; the exemption is stated and priced: on this ridge
                reader a 1024-dim block addition moves the hit rate by
                about -0.0045..+3e-5 per +2048 dims (F-16 P1, the measured
                dilution) and on this registration's smoke by -0.0004
                (free_all - FREE_BIGRAM) and +0.0003 (HISTORY_BIGRAM -
                history_tok), two orders below the +0.05 floor, so a twin
                could not move a reading; the landing reports those two
                deltas with CIs as the dilution anchors.
  REPORTED    history_tok - the unselected free bigram; free_all -
                FREE_BIGRAM; history_all - free_all; HISTORY_BIGRAM -
                history_tok; history_tok - history; free_bigram_b -
                free_bigram_a; every arm's point and CI at B = 8 / 16 / 32;
                the D_eq and D_add at B = 8 and 32; the lambda table and
                grid-edge flags; table coverage (share of positions whose
                key has no train count, per table, per split).
- LABELS (mechanical; the PRIMARY harvest's label is THE label, the
  replication is computed identically and reported as "agrees / disagrees"
  on the label and on both readings; a disagreement is written out, the
  primary's label stands as F-26's convention):
  REMEASURE-INVALID  the precondition fails on that harvest.
  FREE-HISTORY       D_eq not SIGNAL and D_add not SIGNAL.
  COMPLEMENTARY      D_eq not SIGNAL and D_add SIGNAL.
  SURVIVES           D_eq SIGNAL and D_add SIGNAL.
  READER-INCONSISTENT  D_eq SIGNAL and D_add not SIGNAL. D_add - D_eq =
                     HISTORY_BIGRAM - history_tok exactly, so this label is
                     a knife-edge at the floor (D_eq +0.051 with D_add
                     +0.049 would fire it); it is blamed on the reader
                     only if HISTORY_BIGRAM - history_tok has CI95 upper
                     < 0 (the union reader is CI-clear WORSE than its
                     sub-reader), otherwise it is written as a FLOOR
                     STRADDLE in those words. The single shared lambda is
                     NOT presumed the cause: the committed history val
                     curve is flat (0.8093 at lambda 10 against 0.8096 at
                     1000), so sharing one lambda costs history_tok about
                     0.0003 at most.
  INCOMPLETE         a registered arm or label cell is missing.
  Where D_eq or D_add is CI-positive below the floor, or NEGATIVE, the
  outcome text says so in those words beside the label, and the pinned
  sentences use the frozen NOT-SHOWN wording ("no material margin ... is
  shown"), never "no better" or "reproduced".
- CONSEQUENCES (pinned; executed at landing as dated lines, never
  rewrites). EVERY label among FREE-HISTORY / COMPLEMENTARY / SURVIVES /
  READER-INCONSISTENT: a dated STATUS line under F-26 (FINDINGS.md) that
  QUOTES D_eq, D_add and BIGRAM GAIN with their CIs at B = 16, j = 1, names
  the budget and horizon, and carries the pinned sentence of the label
  (the tool's SENTENCES, frozen with the instrument); dated pointers
  beside the SCOPE sentence on every text that carries it (this block's
  OUTCOME, OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-9, FUTURE_IDEAS P1, README, WHY_THIS_DIES [withheld: FUTURE_IDEAS not in this repository; see WITHHELD.md]
  K-6); the predictions scored clause by clause; the share of the
  re-measured margin that the free previous token accounts for reported
  as the point ratio BIGRAM GAIN / re-measured ADDRESS-BEYOND-TOKEN (a
  point ratio, no CI); gate 0's share of the summed gain beside the
  argmax. FREE-HISTORY: the STATUS line adds, in these words, "once the
  free previous token is in the baseline at equal dims, no material
  margin of the address block is shown and no material margin of the
  address stream over the free bigram is shown; the sideband-premise
  reading of F-26's sideband sentence is WITHDRAWN at this reader; the
  sentence stands as a mechanical label about the registered arms"; stage
  2 stays a live OPTION on PREFETCH-HEADROOM (which does not depend on
  this margin) with its address-beyond-free motivation struck.
  COMPLEMENTARY: the STATUS line adds "no material margin of the address
  block over an equal-dims free bigram block is shown; the address stream
  adds [D_add with CI] over the free bigram at this reader, a margin that
  may include previous-token identity the routing exposes and the table
  does not; the F-26 margin was in part free token history ([share])";
  the next free rung is named as unrun and unregistered: a longer free
  history (tokens[t-2]) or a pair-keyed (true bigram) table with its own
  coverage question, the identity-resolving encoding among them.
  SURVIVES: the STATUS line adds "the address block adds [D_eq with CI]
  over an equal-dims free bigram block and [D_add with CI] over the free
  bigram at this reader; the critic's bigram objection is answered at
  THIS ENCODING (two additive 1024-dim train tables), not for previous-
  token information in general"; the same next rung named.
  READER-INCONSISTENT: the STATUS line reports both readings with CIs and
  HISTORY_BIGRAM - history_tok with its CI, writes no sideband sentence,
  and says "reader" only under the CI-upper-below-zero condition pinned
  under LABELS, "floor straddle" otherwise; a per-block-lambda reader is
  named as the next rung only in the "reader" case. REMEASURE-INVALID: the
  run is VOID; no STATUS line on F-26's sentence; a dated note under this
  block records the gap and quotes D_eq / D_add as numbers only, never as
  readings; any rerun needs a new dated registration naming what changed.
  INCOMPLETE: the run is void, no STATUS line; a dated note names the
  missing arm or cell; a rerun needs a new dated note. A grid-edge lambda
  on a label-bearing arm, a disagreement between the replication and the
  primary, a reported readout that disagrees with the label (history_tok
  minus the unselected encoding; history_all - free_all, the strongest
  free baseline here, the F-24 lesson; free_all - FREE_BIGRAM; the B = 8
  or B = 32 readings): each is said in those words beside the label, and
  the label stays. No wall-clock, bytes or latency sentence is licensed
  by any label (D-9; K-5 / K-6 stay UNTESTED whatever the label); no
  label calls D_add "context".
- HONEST PREDICTIONS (both pinned before any registered readout ran; the
  smoke in (b) below was run after they were written and does not revise
  them). THE CRITIC'S (2026-09-15, recorded in the OUTCOME above): the
  margin drops to or below the +0.05 floor, driven by gate 0 — that is,
  D_eq reads NOT-SHOWN (or NEGATIVE) and gate 0 has the largest per-gate
  gain; it implies FREE-HISTORY or COMPLEMENTARY. THE ASSISTANT'S
  (2026-10-01, derived from the committed per-gate numbers and the
  critic's diagnostic, so informed rather than blind): the encoding
  selected is (b) prev_table; FREE_BIGRAM 0.84..0.88 at B = 16 (BIGRAM GAIN
  +0.03..+0.07; gate 0 the largest per-gate gain, at least twice the next
  gate's and at least a quarter of the summed gain; each of the other
  fifteen gates between 0 and +0.04); D_eq +0.03..+0.08, straddling the
  floor, so NOT-SHOWN or a SIGNAL at the floor's edge; D_add +0.05..+0.09,
  SIGNAL; the most likely label COMPLEMENTARY on the primary, SURVIVES
  the alternative; the replication agrees on the label; the precondition
  holds with a gap under 0.003; every lambda interior. The two
  predictions differ only on D_eq's side of the floor; the critic's
  "driven by gate 0" is scored by the argmax, and the share beside it
  says how much of the drop gate 0 carried (its cap, 0.020 of a needed
  0.053, says it cannot have carried most of a drop to the floor).
  WHAT WOULD SURPRISE: D_eq at or above +0.10 (the free previous token
  adds nothing at equal dims); D_eq NEGATIVE (the free block beats the
  address block); D_add NOT-SHOWN (the address stream adds nothing over two
  free tokens — the full free-history null at this reader, the K-2 shape
  one level up); encoding (a) selected over (b); the largest per-gate gain
  anywhere but gate 0; a precondition gap above 0.005.

OQ-9 STAGE-1 GENERALISING FREE BASELINE REGISTRATION (R2) (2026-10-02,
pre-run; a DATED AMENDMENT to the STRATIFIED COVERAGE READ block above,
written BEFORE any readout of it ran on either S3 harvest; the critic's

  [+0.1596, +0.2280] / +0.1741 [+0.1390, +0.2154] on 0.0987 / 0.1418 of

  DIAGNOSTIC on test rows that stage 1, the twin, the stratified read and

  precedent, as the two reads before it). NON-CRITERION for every
  mechanical label in the record: F-26's labels, the twin's SURVIVES and
  the stratified read's FALLBACK-LOCATED / PT-SURVIVES stand as computed;
  no K-* status, no F-15 / F-17 / F-24 / F-25 sentence moves. ONE pinned
  consequence: a dated STATUS line under F-26 (the third) on the standing
  of the twin's coverage caveat against a free encoding that is never at
  the marginal, and on the address margin against the strongest free arm
  this registration builds (the p_t summaries and the full 2,048-wide h_a
  not included; c), per the branches below (a dated line, never a rewrite
  — the 2026-08-31 rule), with dated pointers wherever the caveat or the
  next-rung sentence is carried.
- TWO QUESTIONS, read on the same positions. (Q1, SPARSITY) When the free
  tables are replaced by an encoding that generalises across token keys —
  the model's own routers replayed on the token's input embedding as the
  prior of a smoothed count table, so that an unseen key reads the replay,
  a sparse key reads a shrunk count row and a well-covered key reads its
  table — how much of the twin's free arm's deficit is recovered (the
  SHRINKAGE, the headline), and does the address block still beat the
  equal-dims free block on the unseen-key positions where the stratified
  read located the margin, and pooled? (Q2, HIDDEN) With the forward's own
  final-norm output h_a (the harvest's stored "hidden", the state that
  produced p_t and F-23's exact linear carrier of the full p; free under
  D-5 in the information sense, as p_t's summaries were) in the free arm at
  the address block's width, does the address block still beat the
  equal-dims free block, and does the address stream still add over the
  union? Q2 carries this registration's full free block on both sides of
  its union reading, as F-24's Mt did; F-24's equal-dims partner was an
  alignment-destroyed twin, which this read does not build — a block swap
  of H(t) for S[t] over a shared smoothed bigram instead (c; see
  DISCLOSURES (14)).
- THE FROZEN INSTRUMENTS. tools/run_prefetch_strat.py (sha 39a6cd587492...,
  attested by both committed stratified payloads and pinned by
  tests/test_prefetch_strat_landing.py) is imported by bare module name
  and never edited; the new tool refuses to run unless its LF-normalised
  bytes still hash to that sha, and the stratified tool's own import-time

  tool accumulates the twin's Gram with the twin's own statements on the

  lambdas, read from the committed twin payload through the committed
  stratified payload (encoding and lambdas taken verbatim, not
  re-selected), so those arms are the twin's readers and their stratified
  rows are the stratified read's rows; the test suite asserts their
  weights equal Strat.fit's on a fixture harvest. The stratified read's
  four p_t arms are NOT carried (Q2 of that read is answered).
- DATA. The committed S3 harvests exactly as the stratified read opened
  them (PRIMARY results/real/harvest_moe moe_s0..s7, the verdict harvest;
  REPLICATION harvest_moe_r moe_s8..s11, a SEED replication on the same
  prompts; split prompt_idx % 7; readers fit on train pooled over seeds;
  every number read on the 30 TEST prompts). POSITIONS: the twin's bigram
  positions (t >= 1, t + 1 < row length), horizon j = 1; every arm on every
  position; the six strata and three unions of the stratified read,

  opened for Q2 (the shards re-verified against the committed metas' shas
  when it is opened, c); it was never read by the three reads before this
  one.
- INDEX CONVENTION (the frozen one): forward t has INPUT tokens[t-1], OUTPUT
  p_t, routing S[t] and final-norm state hidden[t]; tokens[t] is sampled
  from p_t. At anchor t the decoder holds S[t], tokens[t], tokens[t-1] and
  hidden[t]; the target is S[t+1], the routing of the forward tokens[t]
  feeds. REPLAY(x) at gate l estimates gate l of the forward x FEEDS, so
  REPLAY(tokens[t]) is aligned with the target and REPLAY(tokens[t-1]) with
  S[t] (one forward before the target; see THE SMOOTHING FAMILY).
- THE REPLAY ENCODING. REPLAY(x) in [0, 1]^1024: for each of the 16 gates
  l, the softmax over the 64 experts of W_l . RMSNorm_l(e_x), where e_x is
  row x of the input embedding, RMSNorm_l(v) = v / sqrt(mean(v^2) + eps)
  times the layer's post-attention norm weight (eps = rms_norm_eps 1e-5),
  and W_l (64 x 2048) is the layer's router — the model's own routing
  function applied to the token's embedding in place of the residual
  stream the router actually sees. At gate 0 the only omitted term is
  layer 0's attention output; deeper, the whole stack. It uses model
  weights only (no train sample, no smoothing parameter), is defined for
  every token id, and is free under D-5 in the information sense (the
  prefetcher runs beside the model whose weights these are). WEIGHTS-ONLY
  FEASIBILITY CHECK (2026-10-02, in session, before this registration; no
  harvest routing target read; the harvests' token-id set and array shapes
  read for a size estimate only): the 16 routers, the 16 norm weights and
  the embedding load from the cached checkpoint's safetensors files in
  0.28 s by a struct-and-numpy parser (BF16 bytes widened to float32, then
  float64; nothing imports torch, transformers or safetensors), the replay
  over the full 50,304-token vocabulary takes 7.99 s, and the harvests use
  23,827 distinct token ids. The RAW-embedding variant (no norm) is
  DROPPED on that check: its softmax is near uniform (top-8 mass 0.1262 to
  0.1285 per gate against 8 / 64 = 0.125), so only the RMSNorm variant is
  registered; its top-8 mass averages 0.2099 to 0.3169 per gate (gate 0 the
  sharpest), and its top-8 sets overlap the raw variant's by 0.7493 at gate
  0 rising to 0.8778 to 0.9165 at gates 8 to 15 (the one choice the
  encoding leaves open, made before any read). CHECKPOINT IDENTITY. The
  harvest metas pin the model id (allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct) and
  the shard bytes, not a checkpoint revision. The Hugging Face cache on
  this box holds ONE snapshot of that model
  (b89a7c4bc24fb9e55ce2543c9458ce0ca5c4650e; weight blobs
  61874210ca7c360f..., 97ae01e3519c52e6..., c523a43b8a17269d...; the weight
  blobs dated 2026-08-30, the index file and the snapshot directory
  2026-08-31 16:18 local; c) and the harvests were committed on 2026-08-31
  (primary,
  808266e) and 2026-09-01 (replication, 83406b1), so the harvests were
  almost surely generated from this snapshot: PROBABLE, not verified, and
  this registration does not pretend otherwise. What IS pinned: the sha256
  over exactly the tensors the replay reads, in a fixed order with each
  tensor's name, dtype and shape — model.embed_tokens.weight, then per
  layer mlp.gate.weight and post_attention_layernorm.weight —
  d8e5770a2d88a8bee02518b3f95a88fed122f9a7ce66ba3183d16fdf39936e63,
  computed twice in session and reproducible. The tool carries it as a
  constant, records the snapshot hash, the blob names and the config
  (hidden 2048, 16 layers, 64 experts, top-8, vocab 50,304, eps 1e-5,
  norm_topk_prob false) in the meta, recomputes the replay at run time
  from the cache and REFUSES to write under results/ unless the measured
  sha equals the pinned one. A mismatch between the harvest's checkpoint
  and the replay's would show as a low REPLAY AGREEMENT (reported, below),
  not silently. Nothing of the replay is committed as data: the state
  rows carry the hits, and --conclude-from needs no cache.
- THE SMOOTHING FAMILY. For a key token x, gate g and expert e, with c the
  train count (TABLE_CUR keyed on tokens[t] with target S[t+1] over the
  frozen instrument's j = 1 train positions; TABLE_PREV keyed on tokens[t-1]
  with target S[t+1] over the bigram train positions — the twin's two
  tables, both read LEAVE-ONE-PROMPT-OUT at train rows exactly as the twin
  reads them), n = the row's count sum at that gate (a train occurrence
  adds 8 counts per gate, so n is 8 times the key's occurrences after the
  leave-one-prompt-out) and r = REPLAY(x) at that gate:
    SMOOTH_k(x)[g, e] = (c + k r) / (n + k)
  a count table with the replay as its Dirichlet prior at weight k, in
  COUNT units: k = 8 is one virtual train occurrence per gate. Limits: k =
  0 is the TABLE where n > 0 and the REPLAY where n = 0 (the BACKOFF
  encoding: the twin's table with the replay in place of the marginal
  fallback); k = inf is the REPLAY everywhere. Every row sums to 1 at every
  gate; a well-covered key is close to its table, a key seen once is pulled
  toward the replay, an unseen key IS the replay, so no free table row is
  ever at the marginal. ONE k for both tables, selected JOINTLY with lambda
  for the free arm on the pooled VAL positions by the twin's rule (hit rate
  at B = 16, strict >, ties keep the smaller k then the smaller lambda;
  grid-edge flagged for k as for lambda). K GRID {0, 2, 8, 32, 128, 512,
  inf} (seven points: the two limits, one quarter of an occurrence to 64
  occurrences). The PREV table's prior is MISALIGNED by one forward (the
  replay of tokens[t-1] estimates S[t], the forward that token fed, while
  TABLE_PREV estimates S[t+1]); it enters as a feature of tokens[t-1] for
  the ridge reader on top, not as a direct estimate, and the one k is
  val-selected over both tables together, so a prior that hurts the PREV
  block costs the free arm at selection (said here, not hidden; a separate
  k per table would square the grid and is declined, see DISCLOSURES).
  Val-selecting k is a fitted scalar in the free arm; the address arm's
  lambda is val-selected too, and the family's limits are reported as
  arms, so the free arm is read at its best over a one-parameter family
  whose ends are the pure table and the pure replay. A registered run
  refuses a stratified payload whose twin encoding is not prev_table (both
  committed payloads carry prev_table), since the smoothed previous-token
  table is TABLE_PREV and the SHRINKAGE would otherwise mix encodings (c).
- THE HIDDEN BLOCK. H(t) in R^1024 from hidden[t] (2048 float16
  coordinates widened to float64): per channel, clipped to the TRAIN
  support (the channel's minimum and maximum over the train bigram
  positions) and z-scored with TRAIN moments (after tools/run_fullfree.py's
  train_moments, F-24's h_a path, which clips to the train support and
  z-scores with an sd floor of 1e-6 over every valid train position; here
  the moments are over the bigram train positions and a zero sd is
  replaced by 1; c, code review), then projected on the 1024 leading
  principal
  directions of the TRAIN covariance of the clipped z-scored channels
  (eigendecomposition in float64, eigenvalues descending, each direction's
  sign fixed so its largest-magnitude coordinate is positive). H carries
  the address block's width (1024) so that the equal-dims comparison is
  exact; it is a REDUCTION of F-24's full block (2048 of 2048 there), a
  limitation said in words wherever Q2's label is quoted. Train moments,
  support and directions never see a val or test row.
- DESIGN. The twin's Gram over the bigram train positions, [S[t] (1024) ++
  TABLE_CUR(tokens[t]) (1024) ++ TABLE_PREV(tokens[t-1]) (1024) ++
  TABLE_CUR(tokens[t-1]) (1024) ++ bias], accumulated by the stratified
  tool's own statement on the same chunks (so the twin's arms reproduce),
  EXTENDED on the same chunks by the Gram blocks the new arms need and no
  others: H(t) (1024) with itself, with S[t] and with the bias; for each k
  of the grid, SMOOTH_k(tokens[t]) ++ SMOOTH_k(tokens[t-1]) (2048) with
  itself, with S[t], with H(t) and with the bias; every block with the
  targets (REPLAY(tokens[t]) and REPLAY(tokens[t-1]) are the k = inf
  blocks). No block is formed between H or a smoothed block and the twin's
  three table blocks, since no arm mixes them; an arm's Gram is assembled
  from the twin's Gram and these blocks, so the twin's nine arms are solved
  from the twin's own Gram and the new arms from blocks accumulated on the
  twin's chunks. Every twin column keeps its index. Readers: the twin's closed-form ridge in float64, every
  coordinate incl. the bias regularised alike; lambdas from the frozen grid
  {0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 1e4, 1e5}; resident set and hit rate as the
  frozen instruments count them; B in {8, 16, 32}, B = 16 the label budget.
- ARMS (dims; k* the selected k; the twin's nine at the twin's lambdas,
  every other arm's lambda selected on the pooled VAL bigram positions,
  strict >, ties keep the smaller, grid-edge flagged):
  the twin's nine — history (1025), free_tok (1025), history_tok (2049),
    free_bigram_b / free_bigram_a (2049), history_bigram_b /
    history_bigram_a (3073), free_all (3073), history_all (4097) — with
    FREE_BIGRAM / HISTORY_BIGRAM the twin's selected encoding (prev_table on
    both committed payloads): the REPRODUCE arms;
  free_r2          SMOOTH_k*(tokens[t]) ++ SMOOTH_k*(tokens[t-1])    (2049)
                   THE generalising free arm, (k, lambda) joint on val;
  history_tok_r2   S[t] ++ SMOOTH_k*(tokens[t])                     (2049)
                   the equal-dims address partner (the twin's structure:
                   both arms share the current-token encoding, the free arm
                   holds the previous token where the address arm holds
                   S[t]);
  history_bigram_r2  S[t] ++ free_r2's blocks                       (3073)
                   the union (the address stream over the free arm);
  free_backoff     free_r2 at k = 0                                  (2049)
  free_replay      free_r2 at k = inf = REPLAY ++ REPLAY             (2049)
                   the family's two ends, each at its own val lambda,
                   REPORTED;
  replay_cur       REPLAY(tokens[t])                                 (1025)
                   the replay alone, REPORTED;
  replay_zerofit   the top-B of REPLAY(tokens[t]) itself, no fit     (none)
                   the FREE_TABLE analogue, REPORTED;
  h_only           H(t)                                              (1025)
  free_h           free_r2's blocks ++ H(t)                          (3073)
                   the strongest free arm this registration builds;
  history_all_h    S[t] ++ free_h's blocks                           (4097)
                   the Q2 union; the Q2 equal-dims address partner of free_h
                   is history_bigram_r2 (3073 against 3073: the swap is S[t]
                   against H(t) over a shared smoothed bigram).
- STATE ROWS: one per (arm, budget, gate, test prompt, STRATUM): hits,
  needed; the header carries the harvest shard shas, the stratified
  payload's path and sha, its state file's sha, the twin record it holds,
  the selected k, the lambdas, and the replay source sha; the meta records
  the BLAS build and the thread caps, the checkpoint snapshot and blob
  names, the k val table, the per-split REPLAY AGREEMENT, the hidden
  block's eigenvalue spectrum summary (the share of train variance the
  1024 directions keep; the 1,024th and 1,025th eigenvalues, the gap at
  the cut, c) and, for eight fixed token ids, the sha256 of each
  token's replay vector bytes (the landing test recomputes them where the
  cache is present). Restricted to the twin's nine arms, the rows are the
  stratified read's rows.
- READOUTS at B = 16 (8 and 32 reported), paired per prompt on identical
  positions within a scope, cluster bootstrap over the 30 test prompts
  (sideband.stats.paired_cluster_delta_ci, n_boot 2000, seed 0; a prompt
  with no position in a scope enters with zero trials), readings by the
  frozen rule (SIGNAL iff CI95 lower > 0 and point >= +0.05, the pinned
  floor; NEGATIVE iff CI95 upper < 0; else NOT-SHOWN):
  PRECONDITION  REPRODUCE: for every (arm, budget, gate, prompt, stratum)
                row of the committed STRATIFIED state file over the twin's
                nine arms, this read's row equals it, hits AND needed, to
                the integer (the stratified read's own rule: EXACT; hits-
                only mismatches on at most 0.1% of those rows, each within
                +-1 hit, REPRODUCE-NEAR said in words; more, any needed
                mismatch, is REPRODUCE-INVALID, void). IDENTITY: the twin's
                D_eq (history_tok - FREE_BIGRAM) on ALL, COVERED and
                FALLBACK, CI included, must equal the stratified payload's
                three cells to 1e-12; otherwise REPRODUCE-INVALID as well.
                NEAR is not a loophole (c): a hits mismatch on a history_tok
                or FREE_BIGRAM row at B = 16 moves the twin's D_eq and fails
                the identity, so NEAR can survive only on the other arms or
                budgets.
  Q1 HEADLINE   SHRINKAGE SHR^s = free_r2 - FREE_BIGRAM on s = FALLBACK,
                COVERED and ALL (and per stratum, reported): what the
                generalising encoding recovers of the twin's free arm's
                deficit, with its CI; SHARE = SHR^FB / D_eq^FB, the free
                arm's gain as a ratio of the stratified read's unseen-key
                margin — not the share of the margin closed, since the
                address arm moves too and D_eq^R2 is the reading that says
                what remains (c) — (a ratio of two points, no CI; undefined
                where the cell is zero; D_eq^FB is the stratified payload's
                cell, reproduced here).
  Q1 GATE       D_eq^R2 = history_tok_r2 - free_r2 on FALLBACK (the scope
                the stratified read located the margin in) and on ALL
                (pooled); on COVERED and per stratum reported. The partner
                is the twin's STRUCTURE, not the twin's arm (c): it carries
                the smoothed current-token block too, so the two arms differ
                only in S[t] against the smoothed previous-token block, and
                the OUTCOME's "the same address arms" is read as the same
                structure; the twin's own address arm against the
                generalising free block, history_tok - free_r2 (2049 against
                2049), is REPORTED per scope beside it (c).
  Q1 UNION      D_add^R2 = history_bigram_r2 - free_r2 on ALL and FALLBACK
                (reported).
  Q2 GATE       D_eq^H = history_bigram_r2 - free_h on ALL (3073 against
                3073; H(t) against S[t] over the shared smoothed bigram).
  Q2 UNION      D_add^H = history_all_h - free_h on ALL (what the address
                stream adds OVER the strongest free arm). D_add^H - D_eq^H =
                history_all_h - history_bigram_r2 exactly, the dilution
                anchor, reported with its CI.
  REPORTED      per scope and on ALL: free_backoff - FREE_BIGRAM and
                free_replay - FREE_BIGRAM (the family's ends against the
                table), free_r2 - free_backoff and free_r2 - free_replay
                (what the selected k adds over each end), replay_cur -
                free_tok and replay_zerofit - free_tok (the replay alone
                against the one-token table), history_tok_r2 - history_tok
                (what the smoothed current-token block adds to the address
                arm; the Q1 analogue of a dilution anchor), h_only -
                free_tok and h_only - history_tok (the hidden block alone
                against the one-token table and against the address arm),
                free_h - free_r2 (what H adds to the free arm), D_eq^R2 and
                D_eq^H per scope, the twin's D_eq and D_add per scope
                (reproduced), every arm's point and CI; each scope's share
                of the test positions; the k val table (seven k by seven
                lambdas, pooled val hit at B = 16) with the selected pair
                and both grid-edge flags; every other arm's lambda table
                and grid-edge flag; REPLAY AGREEMENT per split and per
                gate: the mean overlap of the top-8 of REPLAY(tokens[t-1])
                with S[t] over 8 (the replay against the routing of the
                forward the token actually fed, no fit, no target of any
                readout), and the same for REPLAY(tokens[t]) against
                S[t+1]; the hidden block's kept-variance share; B = 8 / 32
                for every delta.
  FLOOR STRADDLE  every label-bearing reading carries a flag set when its
                CI95 contains +0.05. A flag on the Q1 GATE on FALLBACK, or
                on EITHER Q2 reading, selects the pinned sentence for that
                question that claims nothing beyond the rule ("not settled
                at this power" in those words); a flag on the Q1 GATE on
                ALL, on a SHRINKAGE reading or on the Q1 UNION is said in
                words beside the sentence and selects nothing (the tool
                carries all three as flags, c). The reading itself follows
                the rule and the label stays.
- LABELS (mechanical; the PRIMARY harvest's label is THE label, the
  replication computed identically and reported as agrees / disagrees on
  each question; a disagreement is written out):
  REPRODUCE-INVALID  the precondition or the identity fails on that harvest
                     (void: deltas as NUMBERS, reading fields and both
                     question labels null, straddle flags kept as flags).
  INCOMPLETE         a registered arm or label cell is missing (void).
  Q1  R2-FALLBACK-SURVIVES  D_eq^R2 on FALLBACK SIGNAL.
      R2-POOLED-ONLY        D_eq^R2 on FALLBACK not SIGNAL and on ALL SIGNAL.
      R2-ABSORBED           neither SIGNAL.
      A NEGATIVE reading is "not SIGNAL" and is said in those words.
  Q2  H-SURVIVES        D_eq^H SIGNAL and D_add^H SIGNAL.
      H-COMPLEMENTARY   D_eq^H not SIGNAL and D_add^H SIGNAL.
      H-ABSORBS         neither SIGNAL.
      H-INCONSISTENT    D_eq^H SIGNAL and D_add^H not SIGNAL — a knife-edge
                        at the floor; blamed on the reader only if the
                        dilution anchor has CI95 upper < 0; otherwise, where
                        a Q2 CI95 contains the floor, written as a FLOOR
                        STRADDLE in those words, and otherwise as "neither"
                        (c).
  The label is written Q1 / Q2 (for instance R2-FALLBACK-SURVIVES /
  H-ABSORBS). Where a delta is CI-positive below the floor the text says so
  in the frozen NOT-SHOWN wording ("no material margin ... is shown"), never
  "no better", "reproduced" or "accounted for"; "absorbs" names the label,
  not a mechanism; "sparsity" is a label word for the Q1 ABSORBED branch
  only in the pinned sentence below, which says what was shown, not why.
- CONSEQUENCES (pinned; executed at landing as dated lines, never
  rewrites). EVERY non-void outcome: a dated STATUS line under F-26
  (FINDINGS.md) that QUOTES SHR^FB, SHR^COV, SHR^ALL and the SHARE, D_eq^R2
  on FALLBACK and ALL, D_add^R2 on ALL, D_eq^H, D_add^H and the anchor,
  history_tok - free_r2 on ALL and FALLBACK, history_tok_r2 - history_tok
  and free_h - free_r2 on ALL (c, confirmation round), with their CIs at B
  = 16, j = 1, the selected k and both grid-edge flags,
  the points of free_replay, free_backoff, replay_zerofit, h_only and
  free_h, the REPLAY AGREEMENT at gate 0 and its range over gates on test,
  the scope shares, both labels and the pinned sentences below; dated
  pointers beside the next-rung sentence and the caveat on every text that
  carries them (the stratified read's OUTCOME above, the twin's OUTCOME,
  OPEN_QUESTIONS OQ-9, FUTURE_IDEAS P1, README's SP-MoE line, WHY_THIS_DIES [withheld: FUTURE_IDEAS not in this repository; see WITHHELD.md]
  K-6, REPORT, FINDINGS_INDEX, GLOSSARY); both predictions scored clause by
  clause; a landing test that fails rather than skips on missing committed
  evidence (the cache-dependent replay check skips where the cache is
  absent and says so); the new tool joins the frozen closure (ruff
  force-exclude; CLAUDE.md's count nine attested of twelve). STRADDLE RULE:
  where the Q1 gate on FALLBACK, or either Q2 reading, straddles the floor
  on the primary, the STATUS line uses the straddle sentence (the True
  variants below) in place of the branch's claim; the mechanical label
  stays and is quoted as such. DISAGREEMENT RULE (the stratified read's,
  verbatim in effect): where the replication disagrees with the primary on
  a question, the STATUS line adds "the replication disagrees on [Q1 /
  Q2]: [its label and its readings with CIs]; the primary's label is the
  label and the question is not settled across seeds at this power", and
  the branch's claim for that question is not written.
  LAST RUNG (pinned here, before any read, by the operator's confirmation):
  R2 closes the free-baseline ladder under F-26 (one-token table -> free
  bigram -> stratified read -> generalising baseline with the hidden arm).
  No further free-baseline rung is registered on this margin WHATEVER the
  labels: a SURVIVES label is written "at this reader, against the free
  arms this registration builds (the p_t summaries and the full h_a not
  included), with H at 1024 of 2048 dimensions" (c) and the next
  move is the write-ups or stage 2 under its own registration, never an
  R3; an ABSORBED label is written as the end of the ladder. The one
  exception is a VOID run (REPRODUCE-INVALID or INCOMPLETE), which licenses
  a rerun under a dated note naming what changed, not a new rung.
  Q1 R2-FALLBACK-SURVIVES (no straddle): "against a free encoding that is
  never at the marginal (the model's own routers replayed on the token
  embedding as the prior of the smoothed count tables, k = [k*]), the
  address block still adds a material margin over the equal-dims free
  block on the unseen-key positions ([D_eq^R2 on FALLBACK with CI]; pooled
  [D_eq^R2 on ALL with CI]), while the encoding recovers [SHR^FB with CI]
  of hit rate there (the gain-to-margin ratio [SHARE]): the located margin
  is NOT shown to be table sparsity at this encoding
  and the coverage caveat stands as a scoped limitation, not a retraction"
  (straddle on FALLBACK: "the equal-dims margin on the unseen-key positions
  reads SIGNAL by the rule with a CI95 that straddles the +0.05 floor: not
  settled at this power").
  Q1 R2-POOLED-ONLY (no straddle): "no material margin of the address block
  over the equal-dims generalising free block is shown on the unseen-key
  positions ([D_eq^R2 on FALLBACK with CI]) while the pooled margin is
  material ([D_eq^R2 on ALL with CI]): the margin the stratified read
  located on the unseen keys is not shown to survive this encoding", with
  "and what survives sits on the covered positions" added ONLY where
  D_eq^R2 on COVERED reads SIGNAL and "while the unseen-key reading is not
  SIGNAL at this power" otherwise (c: FALLBACK can read NOT-SHOWN through
  CI width while carrying the pooled margin) (straddle on FALLBACK: the
  "not settled at this power" sentence in place of the first clause).
  Q1 R2-ABSORBED (no straddle): "no material margin of the address block
  over the equal-dims generalising free block is shown on the unseen-key
  positions ([D_eq^R2 on FALLBACK with CI]) nor pooled ([D_eq^R2 on ALL
  with CI]), while the encoding recovers [SHR^FB with CI] of hit rate on
  the unseen keys (the gain-to-margin ratio [SHARE]): the margin the
  stratified read located was not shown to survive a free encoding that is
  never at the marginal — consistent with table sparsity, which is what
  this rung was registered to separate; the coverage caveat is resolved in
  the free baseline's favour at this encoding" (straddle on FALLBACK:
  "neither reading is SIGNAL by the rule while the unseen-key CI95
  straddles the +0.05 floor: not settled at this power"). QUALIFIERS (c,
  design round B3): where k* is the grid's pure-replay end, the clause
  "consistent with table sparsity ... in the free baseline's favour" is
  REPLACED by "with k at the pure-replay end of the grid the encoding
  replaced the tables for every key, seen or not, so the absorption is not
  attributable to the sparse keys and the coverage caveat is neither
  resolved nor retired by it"; where k* is not the pure-replay end (k* = 0
  included; c, code review's confirmation) and SHRINKAGE on FALLBACK does
  not read SIGNAL, the sparsity clause is REPLACED by "the
  encoding did not recover a material share of the unseen-key deficit
  (SHRINKAGE on fallback not SIGNAL), so the absorption is not attributed
  to table sparsity" (c, code review: an absorption the free arm did not
  earn is not credited to sparsity); where history_tok_r2 - history_tok on
  ALL or on FALLBACK reads NEGATIVE, the sentence adds "the shared k
  handicaps the address partner (history_tok_r2 reads below history_tok,
  NEGATIVE, on [the scope(s)]), so part of the absorption is that
  handicap, and the twin's own address arm against the generalising free
  block (history_tok - free_r2, reported per scope) is read beside it" (c,
  code review: keyed on FALLBACK too, the gate's scope); the tool composes
  all of it. An ABSORBED
  reading says nothing about F-26's PREFETCH-HEADROOM label (HISTORY and
  INTRA-FORWARD do not depend on this margin) and nothing about context in
  the address stream; it strikes nothing by itself (see Q2).
  Q2 H-SURVIVES (no straddle): "with the forward's final-norm state at the
  address block's width in the free arm, the address block adds a material
  margin over the equal-dims free block ([D_eq^H with CI]) and the address
  stream adds a material margin over the free bigram plus the hidden block
  ([D_add^H with CI]): the address margin survives the strongest free arm
  this registration builds (the p_t summaries and the full h_a not
  included) at this reader, with H at 1024 of 2048 dimensions" (c)
  (straddle: "both Q2 readings are SIGNAL by the rule while at least one
  CI95 straddles the +0.05 floor: not settled at this power").
  Q2 H-COMPLEMENTARY (no straddle): "with the hidden block in the free arm,
  no material margin of the address block over the equal-dims free block
  is shown ([D_eq^H with CI]) while the address stream adds a material
  margin over the free bigram plus the hidden block ([D_add^H with CI])"
  (straddle: the union-SIGNAL, equal-dims-not sentence with "not settled at
  this power").
  Q2 H-ABSORBS (no straddle): "with the hidden block in the free arm, no
  material margin of the address block over the equal-dims free block
  ([D_eq^H with CI]) and none of the address stream over the free bigram
  plus the hidden block ([D_add^H with CI]) is shown: at this reader the
  forward's own final-norm state plus two tokens' smoothed routing
  profiles show no material address margin (NON-CRITERION; K-2 is
  untouched — this is a prefetch hit-rate reader, not the K-2 reader);
  stage 2's address-beyond-free motivation is struck (PREFETCH-HEADROOM,
  which does not depend on this margin, stands)". The stage-2 strike
  applies under this branch ONLY, and only when NEITHER D_eq^H's nor
  D_add^H's CI95 contains the floor AND the replication agrees on Q2 (the
  stratified read's rule for PT-ABSORBS, carried over) AND the READER
  GUARD below did not fire on either harvest (c); where either CI does,
  the straddle sentence replaces the branch's claim and nothing is struck;
  D_add^H's FALLBACK reading is said in words beside any strike, since the
  margin was located there (c). Where D_eq^H is NEGATIVE that is said in
  the words "the address block reads below the equal-dims free block with
  the hidden block (NEGATIVE)", and where D_add^H is NEGATIVE in the words
  "the address stream reads below the free bigram plus the hidden block
  (NEGATIVE)", each reading its own prefix, both where both are (c, code
  review: the first draft used the equal-dims words for either reading,
  the smoke's shape). READER GUARD (c, design round B1): where free_h - free_r2
  on ALL or the dilution anchor history_all_h - history_bigram_r2 on ALL
  reads NEGATIVE (CI95 upper below zero), adding the hidden block degraded
  a reader at this train size; the Q2 label stays mechanical and is
  quoted, but its branch sentence is REPLACED, under every Q2 label, by
  "with the forward's final-norm state at the address block's width in the
  free arm, [the degraded reading, or both readings joined by 'and'] reads
  (read) NEGATIVE: the hidden block degrades a reader at this train size;
  the Q2 label is mechanical and is quoted, but no Q2 branch claim is
  written and nothing is struck" (the tool's wording, conjugated by count;
  c, confirmation round); a NEGATIVE D_eq^H or D_add^H keeps its NEGATIVE
  prefix under the guard (c, confirmation round); a guard that fires is
  said beside the label and names the reading. The smoke tripped it on both readings (free_h -
  free_r2 -0.0661, the anchor -0.0879, under (b)); LAST RUNG forbids a
  rerun, so the guard is pinned here.
  Q2 H-INCONSISTENT: both readings quoted with CIs and the dilution anchor
  with its CI; no sentence on the margin is written; "reader" under the
  CI-upper-below-zero condition pinned under LABELS (the READER GUARD's
  sentence then replaces the branch's), "floor straddle" where a Q2 CI95
  contains the floor, "neither" otherwise (c, confirmation round).
  VOID branches: REPRODUCE-INVALID or INCOMPLETE — no STATUS line; a dated
  note under this block records the gap and quotes the deltas as numbers
  only, never as readings; a rerun needs a new dated registration naming
  what changed. SAID IN WORDS, always, beside the label: a grid-edge k or
  lambda on any arm; a disagreement between the replication and the
  primary on either question; every floor straddle; REPRODUCE-NEAR; a
  NEGATIVE reading; a reported readout that disagrees with its label (the
  B = 8 / 32 readings; free_backoff or free_replay above free_r2 on test
  while val selected k*; h_only above history_tok — the tool carries these
  as flags, c); replay_zerofit at B = 16 on test below stage 1's RECENCY_16
  at j = 1 (0.5197 / 0.5155, results/real/prefetch_s3.json and
  prefetch_s3_r.json: the same budget and the same target S[t+1]), which
  would say the replay alone is a weaker prefetch source than the cache (c:
  the first draft compared the gate-0 top-8 agreement against S[t] to that
  cell, a mismatch of budget and target, and mis-attributed the cell to the
  twin; the comparison is made at landing against the committed stage-1
  cell, and its position sets differ — stage 1's j = 1 positions include
  t = 0, the bigram positions do not — which the landing says; c,
  confirmation round). No wall-clock, bytes or latency sentence is
  licensed by any
  label (D-9; K-5 / K-6 stay UNTESTED whatever the label); no label calls
  any margin "context"; no mechanical label, kill status or finding regime
  moves.
- HONEST PREDICTIONS (pinned before the smoke and before any registered
  readout; the smoke under PRE-FREEZE (b) runs after they are written and
  does not revise them). THE ASSISTANT'S (2026-10-02; informed by the
  committed twin and stratified payloads and by the weights-only check, so
  informed rather than blind): (1) REPRODUCE EXACT on both harvests and
  the identity holds; (2) the selected k is interior, in {8, 32, 128}, and
  free_r2's lambda interior; (3) SHR^FB +0.08..+0.16 SIGNAL; SHR^COV
  +0.000..+0.020 NOT-SHOWN; SHR^ALL +0.010..+0.030 NOT-SHOWN; SHARE
  0.40..0.80; (4) D_eq^R2 on FALLBACK +0.05..+0.14, SIGNAL modal (about
  0.6) with a FLOOR STRADDLE likely; on ALL +0.035..+0.060, NOT-SHOWN
  modal with a straddle; Q1 modal R2-FALLBACK-SURVIVES, R2-ABSORBED the
  alternative, R2-POOLED-ONLY unlikely; (5) history_tok_r2 - history_tok
  on ALL +0.003..+0.015, on FALLBACK +0.02..+0.08 (the address arm gains
  from the smoothed current-token block where its table was at the
  marginal too); (6) free_replay pooled 0.66..0.80 at B = 16, below
  FREE_BIGRAM's committed 0.8534 / 0.8449; replay_zerofit 0.45..0.65;
  replay_cur at or below free_tok's 0.8110 / 0.8035; free_backoff within

  0.55..0.80, falling with depth to 0.25..0.45 over gates 8 to 15; (8)
  h_only 0.85..0.93 at B = 16 and within +-0.03 of history_tok's 0.9143 /
  0.9109; D_eq^H on ALL -0.03..+0.02 (NOT-SHOWN or NEGATIVE; SIGNAL
  unlikely); D_add^H +0.005..+0.035 NOT-SHOWN; the anchor +0.000..+0.020;
  Q2 modal H-ABSORBS (about 0.6), H-COMPLEMENTARY the alternative (about

  on both labels; (10) the hidden block's 1024 directions keep at least

  below free_tok; SHR^FB NOT-SHOWN; k* at a grid end (0 or inf); any

  (REPLAY AGREEMENT, replay_zerofit) transfer and whose fitted arms do not;

  on FALLBACK +0.05..+0.12, SIGNAL modal (about 0.6), straddling in about

- DISCLOSURES. (1) The test rows have been read four times before this
  registration (stage 1, the twin, the stratified read, the critic's
  recomputes); this diagnostic re-reads them with registered readers,
  registered before the readout, on the F-24 twin-inertness precedent; the
  REPRODUCE arms repeat numbers already read and are identity checks, not
  new readings. (2) The design — the replay encoding, the smoothing
  family and its grid, the hidden block's reduction, the arms, the gates,
  the labels and the sentences — is the assistant's construction from the
  stratified read's one-sentence next rung; the operator confirmed the
  order and the hidden arm; the critic's design round reviews it before
  the freeze and its amendments are marked (c). (3) The weights-only
  feasibility check (THE REPLAY ENCODING) read model weights, the harvests'
  array shapes and their token-id set; no routing target, no val or test
  row's routing, no hit rate. Its outputs are scratch, not evidence; the
  numbers quoted above are the record of what decided the raw-versus-norm
  choice. (4) The smoke under (b) runs on replication shard moe_s8's VAL
  prompts re-split three ways, to a scratch path outside results/, with
  --strat none (no committed payload is read under a smoke, so REPRODUCE
  is not applicable there and the twin's arms take val-selected lambdas
  and a val-selected encoding, the twin's own rule), the replay from the
  cache and both grids in full; it calibrates the runtime and reads the
  REPLAY AGREEMENT on val rows first; it is disclosed with its numbers
  under PRE-FREEZE and revises no prediction. (5) PRIOR ART, verified by
  web search on 2026-10-02 (ids to re-verify before any external
  citation): Eliseev and Mazur 2023 (arXiv 2312.17238) prefetch by
  applying the NEXT layer's gate to the PREVIOUS layer's hidden state — the
  cross-layer cell F-26's INTRA-FORWARD reading occupies, not this
  encoding; Pre-gated MoE (Hwang et al., ISCA 2024, arXiv 2308.12066)
  trains a pre-gate at the previous layer, cross-layer again; SiDA-MoE
  (arXiv 2310.18859) trains an offline LSTM hash from token embeddings to
  every layer's experts — the nearest cell to a replay from the embedding,
  trained where this is not; three 2025-2026 prefetching papers surfaced
  in the same search (arXiv 2511.05814, 2605.11537, 2606.15453) and are
  unread. The replay is a free BASELINE here; no novelty is claimed for
  it, and none is needed. (6) The PREV table's prior is misaligned by one
  forward (THE SMOOTHING FAMILY); a separate k per table (a 49-point grid)
  is DECLINED for the grid's size; a hashed-table encoding (the OUTCOME's
  other candidate) is NOT run — the replay already gives every key a
  non-marginal row, which is what a hash would buy — and is named here as
  the unrun alternative. One lambda per arm spans blocks of different scale
  (a multi-hot, probability rows, H), the frozen convention (c). (7) The raw-embedding replay variant is dropped
  on the weights-only check (near-uniform softmax), a choice made before
  any routing was read. (8) Q2 reduces h_a to 1024 principal directions:
  F-24's block was 2048 wide, and a 2048-wide H against the 1024-wide
  address block would not be equal dims; the reduction is a limitation of
  Q2's SURVIVES branch, said in its sentence; the kept-variance share is
  reported. (9) Multiplicity: four label-bearing readings (D_eq^R2 on
  FALLBACK and ALL; D_eq^H; D_add^H) and one precondition at the label
  budget; the SHRINKAGE readings are the headline numbers but bear no
  label; everything else reported; the replication is the insurance.
  (10) Memory and runtime: the hidden array is 1.76 GB in float16 for the
  primary harvest and is kept in float16 until each chunk; the twin's
  4,097-column Gram is 134 MB in float64 and each k's block set about 84
  MB (seven of them); the box has 31.8 GB. (11)
  Evidence files are written with LF newlines on every platform. (12) The
  new tool's sha is attested in its payloads, so at landing it joins the
  frozen instruments (ruff force-exclude; CLAUDE.md nine attested of
  twelve). (13) Where the Hugging Face cache is absent (CI, a fresh clone)
  the registered runs cannot be repeated, by design: the replay is model
  weights the record does not ship; --conclude-from, the landing test's
  recompute and every label need only the state file. (14) (c) D_add^H has
  no alignment-destroyed twin: the dilution anchor history_all_h -
  history_bigram_r2 is the only check on what H adds to the address arm,
  and the H-SURVIVES branch is scoped to it; the union reading would not
  need H cut to 1024 but is read at the same H so that one reader serves
  both Q2 readings. (15) (c) The eight replay-probe shas depend on the
  payload's replay_vocab and the tool's 4,096-row chunk (the chunking moves
  the last bits), so the landing test recomputes them at the payload's
  replay_vocab with that chunk.

  No new real-data contact before this registration beyond the committed

  prefetch_r2_s3_r.json, prefetch_s3.json, prefetch_s3_r.json, read in
  session on 2026-10-04); no harvest array, val row or test row was opened
  before the HONEST PREDICTION was written (the smoke under (b) opened
  moe_s8's val rows after it; c, A11).
  (4) The smoke under (b) runs on replication shard moe_s8's VAL prompts
  re-split three ways, to a scratch path outside results/, with --r2 none
  (no committed payload is read under a smoke, so REPRODUCE is not
  applicable there and every selection is val's), the replay from the cache
  and both grids and all four horizons in full; it calibrates the runtime
  and exercises the horizon tables on real token ids; it is disclosed with
  its numbers under PRE-FREEZE and revises no prediction; its tables are
  undertrained (the stage-1 smokes' caveat), so its labels are not
  predictive of the registered runs. (5) MULTIPLICITY: six label-bearing
  readings (D_eq^H and D_add^H at three horizons) and one precondition, and
  the stage rule fires SURVIVES on ANY of three horizons. The exposure is
  not a per-horizon false-SIGNAL rate (c, A5): SIGNAL needs a CI95 lower
  bound above zero AND a point at or above the absolute +0.05 floor on BOTH
  cells, the CI half-widths at B = 16 are about 0.004 at horizon 1 (R2's
  committed cells), far below the floor, and the three horizons are
  strongly positively correlated (the same prompts, nested positions), so
  "independent 5% per horizon" is the wrong model. The real exposure is a
  true margin near +0.05 at one horizon crossing the floor by sampling; the
  straddle rule withholds the claim there and the cross-harvest conditions
  under CONSEQUENCES (the replication at the same j) are the insurance. No
  two-horizon rule and no Bonferroni floor is pinned (the critic's ruling);
  said here, not hidden. (6) The TREND across horizons sits on
  nested, different position sets with no pairing; it is reported as a
  description and carries no reading and no CI; the registered claims are
  per horizon. (7) PRIOR ART: F-26 pinned the prefetch cells as occupied
  (address-only history tables, cross-layer routing predictors,
  draft-conditioned prefetch; docs/PRIOR_ART.md) and R2's round added the
  replay's neighbours; the multi-step-ahead (lead-time) expert-prediction
  cell was NOT re-searched for this registration — the value is the
  measurement on this model against the record's own free arms, as F-26
  pinned, and no novelty is claimed. (8) Memory and runtime: per horizon
  the Gram blocks are rebuilt (the twin's 4,097-column Gram, 134 MB, and
  seven k block sets of about 84 MB) and freed; the horizon's two tables
  ((vocab, 16, 64) int64, about 412 MB each at vocab 50,304) are freed once
  the horizon is read, the horizon-1 tables kept; the hidden array is kept
  in float16 as R2 keeps it; the box has 31.8 GB. (9) Evidence files are
  written with LF newlines on every platform. (10) Where the Hugging Face
  cache is absent the registered runs cannot be repeated, by design (the
  replay is model weights the record does not ship); --conclude-from, the
  landing test's recompute and every label need only the state files and
  the committed R2 files. (11) The horizon-matched tables are a design
  choice this registration makes and names; the alternative (horizon-1
  tables at every horizon, stage 1's choice) is NOT run — a comparison of
  the two free encodings at j >= 2 would be a new free-baseline rung, which
  NO FURTHER RUNG forbids; the choice is defended under INDEX CONVENTION and
  the horizon-matched ABT is set beside stage 1's committed cells at
  landing as a description. The critic's ruling (c, A7): the comparison is
  fair in both directions — the smoothed blocks are shared by both sides of
  D_eq^H and D_add^H, only S[t] against H(t) differs and both are read
  linearly at t; in population E[S[t+j] | token] dominates any other
  function of the token as a free feature, so the horizon-matched table is
  the right free encoding and the horizon-1 alternative is rightly
  declined; what remains is the misaligned replay prior, whose bias points
  toward ABSORBED on the fallback scope (H(t), which carries p_t, plausibly
  compensates for unseen tokens better than S[t]) and is bounded by the
  fallback share (0.0987 / 0.1418 of the test positions at horizon 1),
  which is why the fallback readings are quoted beside every closing line.

- THE QUESTION. At this pair and regime, how much does a change of the
  sampling seed under the SAME policy move the pooled tokens/call estimand
  on the SAME prompts, as a function of the number of prompts; how reliable
  is one seed's per-prompt tokens/call as a measure of the prompt; and how
  often does seed noise alone clear the +0.062 bar and a single comparator
  leg of the F-19 WIN rule at the sizes the record has used (30 val prompts;
  42 test-prompt clusters; 84 held-out prompts; 126; 210 verdict prompts)?
  WHICH NULL THIS IS (c, B3): a CROSS-SEED, same-policy, SINGLE-COMPARATOR
  null. The record's gate legs are SAME-SEED (D-6: every arm of a verdict
  set runs at one seed, the per-prompt streams from SeedSequence(seed).spawn;
  F-19's three legs at seed 1, F-21's at seed 3) and ALL-COMPARATOR (every
  leg must hold). A no-effect policy at the same seed is bit-identical to
  its comparator until its first divergent decision, so the same-seed null's
  noise lies between zero and the cross-seed noise measured here FOR A
  POLICY WHOSE PER-PROMPT TOKENS/CALL VARIANCE DOES NOT EXCEED VANILLA'S
  (same-seed Var(y_P - y_V) = Var(y_P) + Var(y_V) - 2 Cov against cross-seed
  2 Var(y_V)); the record's tested arms are adaptive stop / extend policies,
  so that condition is not given. This registration therefore prices what
  is PLAUSIBLY an upper bound on the noise the record's legs faced (argued
  from the shared prefix under that condition; not measured; c, B9 of the
  confirmation round), and the same-seed null itself is NOT measured. The
  experiment that would price it — the first-divergence index per prompt
  between a same-seed arm pair's committed gen.jsonl — is a named,
  unregistered residual (c). No sentence
  about any tested arm follows: the four runs are vanilla, and the verdict
  arms' own cross-seed variance stays unmeasured (one registered seed each).

  2026-10-04) and their metas (seed 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 and the prompt file's

- ESTIMAND. E6's (stage-E clarification E6; tools/e6_gate.py): tokens/call
  on a prompt set P at seed s = sum n_emitted / sum n_blocks over P; the
  NULL DELTA on P = tpc_A(P) - tpc_B(P), A the LOWER seed of the pair (0 and
  2), B the higher (1 and 3); its CI95 by sideband.stats.paired_ratio_delta_ci
  (joint prompt-cluster bootstrap, n_boot 2000, seed 0, percentile) exactly
  as e6_gate, F-19 and F-21 compute a gate leg, the subset's rows passed in
  ascending prompt order (the bootstrap is positional; c, A7); budget dpe_s(P)
  = sum n_drafted / sum n_emitted; the pairwise budget guard: the tested
  arm's dpe <= the comparator's + 0.01 (GLOSSARY, "Pairwise budget guard").
  GUARD IDENTITY (c, B1): between fixed-gamma-4 vanilla runs n_drafted = 4
  n_blocks on every prompt, so dpe = 4 / tokens-per-call on any subset, the
  arm with the higher tokens/call always has the lower budget, every row
  with a positive delta passes the guard, and the guarded rates EQUAL the
  unguarded ones by algebra; the guard is computed and reported as an
  IDENTITY CHECK (the tool records guard_identity_holds per n), never as a
  separate reading. The per-prompt tokens/call y[p, s] = n_emitted /
  n_blocks of prompt p at seed s (the summaries' per-prompt field, identical
  to the ratio to 1e-12).
- READOUTS (per population; every number from all 210 prompts, no split):
  (R1) RELIABILITY: Pearson r between y[., A] and y[., B] over the 210
       prompts; CI95 by a prompt bootstrap (2000 draws with replacement over
       prompts, percentile, the tool's own np.random.default_rng(0), one
       generator per population; the CI half-width is (hi - lo) / 2; c, A2);
       beside it r per family (70 prompts each) and the WITHIN-FAMILY r (both
       series centred on their own family means per seed), reported without
       CIs (c, A9: the pooled r includes between-family variance); the sd of
       y over the 420 prompt-runs (ddof 0) and the mean |y_A - y_B|.
  (R2) VARIANCE DECOMPOSITION of y over the 420 prompt-runs, nested sums of
       squares: SS_total = sum (y - ybar)^2; SS_seed = sum_p sum_s (y[p,s] -
       ybar_p)^2 (seed within prompt); SS_prompt = sum_p 2 (ybar_p -
       ybar_f(p))^2 (prompt within family); SS_family = sum_f 140 (ybar_f -
       ybar)^2. Reported two ways (c, B2): (i) SS / 420 and the SS SHARES of
       SS_total (ML normalisation, no ddof; with two seeds per prompt
       SS_seed / 420 estimates HALF the seed variance and the other half sits
       inside SS_prompt / 420, so the seed SS share reads about (1 - r) / 2
       and is NOT a variance component); (ii) the balanced nested
       METHOD-OF-MOMENTS components, df 210 / 207 / 2: sigma^2_seed =
       SS_seed / 210; sigma^2_prompt = (SS_prompt / 207 - SS_seed / 210) / 2;
       sigma^2_family = (SS_family / 2 - SS_prompt / 207) / 140, with their
       shares of the three-component total. A negative component is
       reported as computed and said in words, never clipped, and the MoM
       shares are undefined (null) unless all three are >= 0; the family
       term has two degrees of freedom and is a FIXED effect of three named
       families, so its "component" is a descriptive variance of three
       means. The identity SS_total = SS_seed + SS_prompt + SS_family to 1e-9
       relative is a PRECONDITION. Family means per seed and pooled are
       reported.
  (R3) HALF-WIDTH vs n, n in {30, 42, 84, 126, 210}: for n < 210, M = 1000
       subsets of n prompts drawn WITHOUT replacement (the tool's own
       np.random.default_rng(1), one generator per population, the n values
       drawn in ascending order so the two populations' subsets share their
       index draws), each subset SORTED before the bootstrap (c, A7); at n =
       210 the one full set. For every subset: delta, lo, hi from
       paired_ratio_delta_ci on that subset's rows; the half-width (hi - lo)
       / 2; dpe_A and dpe_B. Reported per n: median, mean, 5th and 95th
       percentile of the half-width; at n = 210 the single half-width (the
       power note's cell, now a registered number).
  (R4) NULL EXCEEDANCE of the bar at each n over the same subsets: f_plus =
       P(delta >= +0.062) (A over B), f_minus = P(delta <= -0.062) (B over
       A), f_two = f_plus + f_minus = P(|delta| >= 0.062), and the ONE-SIDED
       NULL WIN RATE f_one = f_two / 2 (under the null which seed is "the
       tested arm" is arbitrary — the seed labels are exchangeable — so the
       symmetrised rate is the honest one-sided rate; with the full-set
       delta positive on both populations it is EXPECTED to be stricter

       f) / M); for the halved rates f_one, g_one and g_one^g, SE = HALF the
       SE of the matching two-sided count rate. THE SUBSAMPLING CAVEAT, with
       its
       direction (c, B7): the subsets are overlapping draws WITHOUT
       replacement from ONE set of 210 prompts, so (i) every subset's delta

  +0.0182] / +0.0173 [+0.0133, +0.0221] and at L2 +0.0206 [+0.0171, +0.0244]
  / +0.0207 [+0.0168, +0.0249] (results/real/probes_s3.json and
  probes_s3_replication.json; c, B5): every L3 lens coarsens L2, so F-17's
  DISTINCTIVE claim is the growth from about +0.02 at L2 to about +0.07 at
  L3, and a balanced lens that reads at L2's level would still clear the
  +0.005 floor. THE OPERATOR'S PROGRAM (2026-10-04, "confirm"; 2026-10-05,
  "fold item 2 into item 3"): the noise floor (F-27, landed) -> this
  registration -> the negative-result report. NON-CRITERION for F-26 and
  F-27; CRITERION-BEARING for K-2's status at S3 and for the F-24 / F-25 S3
  cells through the consequence rules below (the OQ-17 / OQ-18 pattern);
  F-17's L3 headline gains a dated lens note and is never rewritten.
- THE QUESTION, two halves on the same harvests and the same frozen chain.
  LENS: through ONE size-capped grouping of the same 510 concepts, pinned
